memory_update.text: Core grid-node public universe should start with PWR, GEV, ETN, HUBB, MTZ, MYRG, POWL, PRIM, EME, NVT, ACM, J, ABB, SMNEY, and AEP.

The strongest direct exposures are grid EPC/labor capacity, transformers, switchgear, substations, HVDC, and utility T&D components; second-order exposures include engineering, permitting, program management, site electrical construction, and regulated transmission owners.
Need deeper verification of grid-specific revenue materiality for ACM, EME, NVT, and J; their inclusion is plausible but less direct than PWR, GEV, HUBB, ETN, MTZ, MYRG, and POWL.

Potential additional candidates not included due to the 15-name cap: ITRI for grid-edge intelligence and distribution visibility, SBGSY for Schneider Electric ADR electrification exposure, DUK/SO/EXC/FE for regulated grid capex, and FCX/SCCO for copper as a second-order materials bottleneck.

Falsification plan: downgrade the node if interconnection queues clear faster than expected, transformer/switchgear lead times normalize, utility capex is disallowed by regulators, or EPC backlogs convert at weak margins because of labor, materials, or fixed-price execution risk.

node: Transmission, interconnection, substations, transformers, switchgear, and grid construction
summary: Expanded U.S.-listed universe for the grid chokepoint node. The highest-relevance candidates cluster into four groups: grid EPC and construction labor capacity, high-voltage and medium-voltage electrical equipment, substation/grid-edge components and software, and regulated transmission owners whose capex cycles create demand. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list. Key falsification points are whether backlog converts to revenue without margin erosion, whether supply shortages only delay revenue, whether utilities face regulatory disallowances on capex, and whether interconnection reform reduces bottleneck scarcity faster than expected.
